bacterial_blight.name: Bacterial Blight
bacterial_blight.description: A bacterial cotton disease that can damage leaves, stems and bolls, especially in warm and humid conditions.
bacterial_blight.symptoms: Angular water-soaked leaf spots that become dark, vein blackening, stem lesions, and dark sunken spots on bolls.
bacterial_blight.treatment: Remove badly infected residues, avoid field work while plants are wet, and ask a local crop specialist about locally approved bactericide or copper-based options.
bacterial_blight.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed, resistant varieties, crop rotation, balanced fertilizer and clean field tools.

curl_virus.name: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus
curl_virus.description: A viral disease commonly spread by whiteflies that reduces plant growth and yield.
curl_virus.symptoms: Upward or downward leaf curling, thickened veins, leaf-like growths under leaves and stunted plants.
curl_virus.treatment: There is no direct cure for an infected plant. Remove severely affected plants where practical and manage whiteflies using locally recommended integrated pest-management methods.
curl_virus.prevention: Grow resistant varieties, control weeds and alternate hosts, monitor whiteflies early and avoid unnecessary insecticide use.

brown_rust.name: Wheat Brown Rust
brown_rust.description: A fungal leaf-rust disease that can spread rapidly when susceptible wheat experiences suitable moisture and temperature.
brown_rust.symptoms: Small orange-brown powdery pustules scattered mainly across the upper leaf surface.
brown_rust.treatment: Confirm the disease in the field and consult a local agriculture specialist about a registered wheat fungicide when crop stage and disease pressure justify it.
brown_rust.prevention: Use resistant varieties, remove volunteer wheat, sow at the recommended time and monitor fields for early rust development.

yellow_rust.name: Wheat Yellow Rust
yellow_rust.description: A fungal rust disease that can reduce photosynthesis and grain yield, particularly in cool and moist conditions.
yellow_rust.symptoms: Yellow-orange powdery pustules arranged in narrow stripes parallel to the leaf veins.
yellow_rust.treatment: Verify the symptoms across the field and seek local advice on a registered fungicide if the disease is active and economically important.
yellow_rust.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, avoid very early sowing where risky, remove volunteer wheat and scout during cool humid weather.

bacterial_leaf_blight.name: Rice Bacterial Leaf Blight
bacterial_leaf_blight.description: A bacterial rice disease that enters through wounds or leaf openings and can spread with rain and irrigation water.
bacterial_leaf_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked streaks near leaf tips or margins that enlarge, turn yellow and then become straw-colored with wavy edges.
bacterial_leaf_blight.treatment: There is no dependable curative spray. Avoid excess nitrogen, improve drainage where possible and consult local extension staff for approved management guidance.
bacterial_leaf_blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties and clean seed, avoid plant injury, maintain field sanitation and apply balanced fertilizer.

brown_spot.name: Rice Brown Spot
brown_spot.description: A fungal disease often associated with infected seed, stressed plants or nutrient-poor soil.
brown_spot.symptoms: Round to oval brown lesions with a gray or pale center, sometimes surrounded by a yellow halo.
brown_spot.treatment: Improve crop nutrition and water management, use clean seed in future crops, and obtain local advice before applying any registered fungicide.
brown_spot.prevention: Use certified seed, treat seed where locally recommended, maintain balanced soil fertility and remove infected residues.

leaf_blast.name: Rice Leaf Blast
leaf_blast.description: A fungal rice disease favored by prolonged leaf wetness, high humidity and susceptible varieties.
leaf_blast.symptoms: Diamond- or spindle-shaped lesions with gray centers and brown or reddish margins.
leaf_blast.treatment: Reduce avoidable crop stress and seek local guidance on a registered blast fungicide if disease pressure and crop stage require control.
leaf_blast.prevention: Use resistant varieties and clean seed, avoid excessive nitrogen, manage plant spacing and prevent long periods of leaf wetness.

tungro.name: Rice Tungro
tungro.description: A viral disease complex spread mainly by green leafhoppers that can cause severe stunting and yield loss.
tungro.symptoms: Yellow to orange leaf discoloration, stunted plants, reduced tillering and delayed flowering.
tungro.treatment: There is no cure for infected plants. Remove infection sources where practical and manage leafhopper vectors using locally recommended integrated methods.
tungro.prevention: Use resistant varieties, synchronize planting, remove volunteer rice and weeds, and monitor leafhopper activity early.
